title: Belding → Fruitport
changes: The driver owns every shot: the driver's Circle fires, R1 picks AIM or LOCKED, the operator's FIRE is gone (#623, 18 Nov). At Belding a manual volley was the operator's FIRE.
The TeleOp launcher keeps spinning between volleys (#661), so a press finds it near speed.
Speed table remeasured on 20245 (#632); aim and launch trim caps (#629), and a fine-trim step on the operator's Circle (#624).
19429's FLOWER stick rebuilt (#635). 20245 stops enforcing the turret's firing arc in TeleOp (#658).
A right-start Auto fires its preloads from RIGHT_AUTO_HIVE (#636).

not_comparable.manual_time: A manual volley was the operator's FIRE at Belding and the driver's Circle at Fruitport: a different press by a different person.
not_comparable.autodrive: With the driver's Circle as the fire button, auto-drive (Square) stopped being the way to launch; the share says what the drive team chose, not how well it worked.
not_comparable.prespun: The TeleOp launcher now keeps spinning between volleys (#661), so 'already at speed' is the new default, not a driver habit.

notes.later: The feed itself: the one number that should not move, and did not.
notes.cycle_full: Fruitport's manual volleys are timed from the driver's Circle (PR #693); Belding's from the operator's FIRE.
notes.cycle_early: As above: the press that starts a manual volley changed.
notes.stuck: #506 detector gate openings that launched nothing while /Lane/Present read a piece. Includes the gate opening during an unjam (feeder reversed), and a rejected NECTAR wedged under the sensor (M-1): checked on video and log, 22 Nov.
notes.slip: Within one robot only: 20245's back-left wheel encoder reads 0 at both events, so its four-wheel mean runs about a quarter low and its ratio about a third high.

19429.nectar_own: 19429 was set to keep only POLLEN on 21 Nov (RobotDifferences: rejectAllNectar), so its reject spits out both NECTAR colours, ours too.
